newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk right-wing party says not joining new govt.
newsitem.headline: Turk right-wing party says not joining new govt.

text.p: A key Turkish far-right party said on Monday it would not join a caretaker government sought by the crumbling Islamist-led coalition, jeopardising the alliance's plans for early elections.
"We have broken off the talks which we have held until now. There is no question of the BBP...joining the government," Grand Unity Party (BBP) deputy chairman Mehmet Ekici told reporters.
The government, which has a razor-thin majority, was relying on the BBP's support to get the necessary parliamentary approval for planned snap polls.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his conservative partner Tansu Ciller announced on June 1 that they were seeking early elections. No date for the polls has been set.

A series of resignations from Ciller's party has eroded the government's majority. Turkey has a hung parliament on paper, but the coalition retains a majority of one as the speaker cannot take part in voting.

However, the coalition is not assured of total support from conservative deputies from Ciller's party unhappy with the failure of their Islamist partners to meet army-led demands for a crackdown on religious activism.
Earlier, the leader of the main opposition Motherland Party said he might bring a censure motion against Erbakan's 11-month-old coalition.

"If the government continues with the same tricks to protect itself, we will propose a censure motion in parliament next week," state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Motherland head Mesut Yilmaz as saying.
Erbakan, under pressure from the secularist establishment, last week announced a plan to hand over power to Ciller.
But negotiations between the coalition partners have become bogged down over the exact details of the swap.
Yilmaz said a censure motion would not be needed if the caretaker government were formed.
